{{short description|French Jesuit priest, geographer and mathematician}}
[[File:Couronne IMG 7007.JPG|thumb|The [[French ship Couronne (1636)|''Couronne'']]. [[Book frontispiece|Frontispiece]] of ''Hydrographie'' by Georges Fournier, 1643.]]
'''Georges Fournier''' (31 August 1595 – 13 April 1652) was a French [[Society of Jesus|Jesuit]] [[Catholic priest|priest]], [[geographer]] and [[mathematician]].

== Biography ==
Fournier served as a naval [[military chaplain]] on a ship of the line,<ref>[http://catalogue.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/cb12138420w/PUBLIC Notice d'autorité de la Bibliothèque nationale de France.]</ref> and acquired a strong knowledge of technical and naval matters.

In 1642, he published the treaty ''Hydrographie'', where he attempted to provide a scientific foundation to the design of ships.<ref>[http://echo.mpiwg-berlin.mpg.de/ECHOdocuView?mode=imagepath&url=/mpiwg/online/permanent/library/6E72TUCT/pageimg&viewMode=images Acessible en ligne sur le site European Cultural Heritage Online]</ref><ref name=Gille>[[Bertrand Gille (historian)|Bertrand Gille]], ''Histoire des techniques''.</ref> At the time, results like [[French ship Couronne (1636)|''Couronne'']] or [[English ship Sovereign of the Seas|''Sovereign of the Seas'']] were obtained by empirical trials and errors.

He also authored a ''Treaty of fortifications or military architecture, drawn from the most estimated places of our times, for fortifications'',<ref name="architectura.cesr.univ-tours.fr">[http://architectura.cesr.univ-tours.fr/Traite/Auteur/Fournier.asp?param= Voir bibliographie et traité en ligne] sur le site ''Architectura'' du Centre d'études supérieures de la Renaissance à [[Tours]].</ref> whose original edition was published in Paris in 1649 by Jean Hénault at the Salle Dauphine of l'ange gardien. Another edition was published in 1668 in Mayence by Louis Bourgeat.<ref>[[:fr:Bibliothèque municipale de Mayence|Bibliothèque municipale de Mayence]], collection Rara III i 30 ba.</ref>

Georges Fournier taught [[René Descartes]].

==Works==
[[file:Georges s.j. fournier, trattato delle fortificazioni o architettura militare, parigi 1654, mont saint michel.jpg|thumb|''Des fortifications...'', 1654]]
In 1642, Fournier published his ''Commentaires géographiques''.<ref name="Taillemite p194">{{harvsp|Taillemite|2002|p=194}}.</ref> The following year he published in Paris the work which will give him the essential part of his celebrity: the ''Hydrographie contenant la théorie et la pratique de toutes les parties de la navigation''.<ref>[http://echo.mpiwg-berlin.mpg.de/ECHOdocuView?mode=imagepath&url=/mpiwg/online/permanent/library/6E72TUCT/pageimg&viewMode=images Accessible en ligne sur le site European Cultural Heritage Online]</ref> Resolutely scientific,<ref name=Gille/> it is the first French maritime [[encyclopedia]].<ref name="Franceschi p624">Michel Vergé-Franceschi, dans {{harvsp|Vergé-Franceschi|2002|p=624}}.</ref> Dedicated to [[Louis XIII]], it was reprinted many times (1667, 1679, 1973). Geographer, astronomer, hydrographer, mathematician, Fournier took an interest in everything: winds and tides, ports, fishing, maritime trade, shipbuilding, the conduct of officers and the art of command.<ref name="Franceschi p624"/> The ''Hydrographie'' was therefore a first-rate source for the history of the navy during the first half of the seventeenth century, which explains the "magnificent re-edition" of this work in 1973 (Etienne Taillemite).<ref name="Taillemite p194"/>
Georges Fournier also published in 1643 a ''Traité de la sphere''<ref name="Franceschi p624"/> and in 1644 a ''Traité de géométrie''.<ref name="Taillemite p194"/> His ''Traité des fortifications ou Architecture militaire'' (published in Paris in 1649 <ref>La deuxième édition est accessible [http://cnum.cnam.fr/CGI/redire.cgi?12RESQE6 en ligne].</ref>) was translated into Dutch, Spanish and German.<ref name="architectura.cesr.univ-tours.fr"/> His works on [[Euclidean geometry]] (Paris, 1644 and 1654) were translated into English, and gave rise to three successive editions.<ref name="Franceschi p624"/> In 1656, posthumously appeared his ''Asiae nova descriptio'' (''New Description of Asia'').<ref name="Franceschi p624"/> The book was made in collaboration with several jesuit missionaries.<ref name="Franceschi p624"/>
